summary: Add a FOREIGN KEY constraint on account_user.referrer_id referencing account_user.id after first resolving orphan referrer_id values by setting them to NULL, deployed via SQL expand stages, then state_only deploy_new, then retire_old.
write_consistency: The old version continues to write referrer_id as integer; setting orphans to NULL ensures FK constraint can be added without violation. The new version reads/writes via ForeignKey; integer column type maintains compatibility during overlap. After retire_old, FK is fully enforced.
revision_notes: Modified expand-fk SQL stage: replaced single ALTER TABLE statement with two sequential statements: first UPDATE orphan referrer_id values to NULL, then ADD FOREIGN KEY constraint. Root cause was orphan referrer_id=1000097 referencing a non-existent account_user row.

stages.description: Clean orphan referrer_id values and add FOREIGN KEY constraint on referrer_id referencing account_user.id.
sql: UPDATE account_user SET referrer_id = NULL WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM account_user u2 WHERE u2.id = account_user.referrer_id);
ALTER TABLE account_user ADD CONSTRAINT referrer_fk FOREIGN KEY (referrer_id) REFERENCES account_user(id);
